newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW -Fisher management to retain stake. [CORRECTED 20:38 GMT]
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW -Fisher management to retain stake. [CORRECTED 20:38 GMT]

text.p: Fisher Scientific International Inc's management will still own stock in the scientific-supply company after completion of Thomas H Lee Co's friendly buyout, Fisher executives said Thursday.

"If it (the deal) does anything, it will raise (management's stake) a little," Paul Meister, the company's chief financial officer, said in an interview with Reuters. He said management currently held about two percent of Fisher's stock outright, or 17 percent including options (corrects from 15 percent).

Under terms of the $1.4 billion recapitalization takeover announced Thursday, 97 percent of Fisher shareholders on a fully-diluted basis will be granted rights to receive $51 per share. The remaining three percent will receive a total of about 10.3 percent of the company.

Fisher began a process to auction the company after Trinity I Fund LP -- an investment group affiliated with the Bass brothers of Fort Worth, Texas -- sent a letter on June 4 to Chief Executive Paul Montrone proposing a leveraged buyout valuing Fisher "perhaps in the range of $47 to $48 per share."
In the letter, Trinity reminded Montrone that it and its associates owned about 10.6 percent of Fisher common stock.
Montrone on Thursday told Reuters Trinity did not participate in the auction process, which yielded three finalists that undertook a due diligence examination of Fisher.
A Trinity spokesman said the investment group declined to particpate, objecting a two-year standstill clause that was part of the confidentiality agreement covering the review of Fisher's documents.

"The standstill agreement would have effectively kept the the Basses from increasing their holding in the company. So we did not examine their internal documents. We found the two-year standstill objectionable," the spokesman said.
He added that Trinity's 10.6 percent equity position in Fisher had not changed.
Montrone said, "Trinity was invited into the process on the same basis as everyone else."

"We hired investment bankers and talked to financial and operating companies. We had indications of interest. We had three institutions that were finalists that did full-scale due diligence," he said.
As for the financing of the Lee recapitalization takeover, Montrone said Chase Manhattan Bank and Merrill Lynch are "fully committed, standing by and ready to go."
He said he expected the transaction to close in November or December.

Under terms of the recapitalization, 90 percent of Fisher equity will be held by a group that includes Thomas H Lee, Chase Capital Partners, DLJ Merchant Banking Partners and Merrill Lynch, Montrone said.
A Thomas Lee spokesman declined to breakout the level of evenutal owneship among the different parties.
